newsitem.title: GERMANY: German opposition motion on sacking Waigel fails.
newsitem.headline: German opposition motion on sacking Waigel fails.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's majority in the German parliament rejected on Wednesday an opposition motion to sack Finance Minister Theo Waigel for trying to have the Bundesbank revalue its gold and pay Bonn the profits.

Waigel pulled back from the controversial plan on Tuesday after the Bundesbank criticised it as a threat to Europe's planned single currency and government deputies said they would refuse to support any infringement of Bundesbank independence.
There were 328 votes against the motion, brought by the Social Democrats (SPD) and Greens, and 311 for it.
"So the motion by the SPD and Greens to sack the finance minister has been rejected," deputy parliamentary spokeswoman Michaela Geiger said.

The vote came after a stormy four-hour debate in parliament in which Kohl threw his weight fully behind the beleaguered Waigel and said Germany would fully meet the strict criteria for European monetary union (EMU) on time.
